purpose: Lower the body as one rigid straight line from a front-support plank position by bending the elbows until the chest is near the floor, then press back up to full arm extension, training chest, shoulder and triceps strength with a stable trunk.

phases.description: Start in high plank with arms extended, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows and lower the body as one unit toward the floor under control.
Chest near the floor, elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees or deeper, body still straight.
Push the floor away, extending the elbows back to the top with the body staying rigid.

faults.description: Hips drop below the shoulder-ankle line so the lower back arches and the body is not a straight line.
faults.cue_intent: Prompt the person to squeeze the abs and glutes to keep hips level with shoulders and heels.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the lower back feels like it is dipping or whether they feel the core tiring.
faults.fix_intent: Suggest bracing the core and glutes, or an easier variation such as incline push-ups, to hold a straight line.

faults.description: Loss of trunk tension, typically late in a set, which lets the hips drift out of line.
faults.cue_intent: Remind to stay tight from head to heels through the whole rep.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask how many reps they have done and whether they are tiring.
faults.fix_intent: Reduce rep count or switch to an easier variation and rest before continuing with good form.

faults.description: Hips rise above the shoulder-ankle line, forming an inverted V that reduces chest loading.
faults.cue_intent: Prompt the person to lower the hips into one line from shoulders to ankles.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they are shifting the hips up to make the movement easier.
faults.fix_intent: Reset the plank with the body in one straight line, then lower while keeping that line.

faults.description: Elbows do not bend enough at the bottom, so the chest stays far from the floor and the rep is partial.
faults.cue_intent: Encourage lowering until the elbows reach about 90 degrees or the chest nears the floor.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the full depth feels too hard or they are stopping early on purpose.
faults.fix_intent: Lower more deeply under control, or use an incline variation to reach full depth with good form.

faults.description: Elbows are not fully extended at the top of the rep.
faults.cue_intent: Cue pressing all the way up until the arms are straight.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they are stopping short to keep tension or because of fatigue.
faults.fix_intent: Finish each rep by fully extending the elbows before starting the next lowering.

faults.description: Upper arms point out far from the body at the bottom, approaching a 90-degree shoulder angle, instead of angled about 45 degrees from the trunk.
faults.cue_intent: Cue tucking the elbows to roughly 45 degrees from the body.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel strain in the front of the shoulders.
faults.fix_intent: Bring the hands slightly lower and the elbows closer to the ribs while lowering.

outcomes.description: Head, hips and heels remain in one straight line throughout the rep.
The rep goes from full arm extension to the chest near the floor and back.
The arms and shoulders move through a stable, efficient pressing path.

links.mechanism: A hip angle near 180 degrees means the trunk and thighs are collinear, so the body acts as a rigid plank.
A deeper elbow bend brings the chest closer to the floor, completing the full range of motion.
Full elbow extension at the top completes the range of motion.
A moderate shoulder angle (elbows about 45 degrees from the trunk) balances chest and triceps loading versus excessive shoulder abduction.
Hands about shoulder width apart set the elbow path; much wider or narrower shifts load between chest and triceps.

session_ideas: Set of 5-10 standard push-ups filmed from the side, with feedback on depth and body line.
Incline push-ups on a bench to practise a straight body line, then progress to the floor.
Tempo push-ups: 3 seconds down, 1 second up, to check control and depth.

vocabulary_proposals.name: angle.shoulder_hip_ankle_line
vocabulary_proposals.why: A direct body-line deviation angle (shoulder-hip-ankle) would assess sagging or piking more robustly than hip angle on the dominant side alone.

vocabulary_proposals.name: height.chest_above_floor
vocabulary_proposals.why: Chest-to-floor distance would measure push-up depth directly rather than inferring it from elbow angle.

vocabulary_proposals.name: angle.elbow_flare_from_trunk_frontal
vocabulary_proposals.why: Elbow flare is best seen from the front; the registry has only a sagittal shoulder angle.
